# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 2 missed 4 of 5 predictions. The naive guess ("same as last round") was closer on all 4 misses, and the fifth row was a tie. So round 3 starts from the round 2 numbers. I change only config C, because F4 gives a specific reason to expect it to move.

Assumption: the round 2 core ticket set has 30 tickets. I use 30 for the trial counts and the cost estimate. I will replace it with the real count when I write the harness.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 2 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows that C never called the outage status check while it was inside the merged tool. Splitting the check back out is the direct fix. It is C's only change this round. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a separate score | A and B are at 0.86, close to the ceiling. The 10 new tickets are scored as a separate "hard set". Results on the round 2 tickets ("core set") then stay comparable with round 2. |
| P3 | Adopt as a default | F6 is still open and D's cost rose from $0.003 to $0.004. Dropping D frees budget for P4. I logged this as a default that you can reverse (see D2 below). |
| P4 | Adopt | B's 0.02 miss is inside noise at 3 trials. With 5 trials per cell, the bands can mean something. |

### Requirement table (goes into `spe/spec/spec.md`, round 3 section)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C calls the outage status check as its own tool. Every other part of C stays as it was in round 2. | r02 F4, P1 | On every outage ticket, C's transcript shows a status tool call. Core-set priority accuracy is measured for C. |
| R3.2 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage. Each has a gold category and a gold priority. | P2 | The hard set has 10 labeled tickets that follow the D1 rule. Results are reported per set. |
| R3.3 | Run configs A, B, and C. Do not run D. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow config list is exactly `[A, B, C]`. |
| R3.4 | Run 5 trials per cell. | P4 | Each cell has at least 5 trials that were not voided, or a logged skip. |
| R3.5 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest case passes. In that case the draft reply says P1 and `label.priority` says P3. The grader must score P3. |
| R3.6 | Make a local commit after each SPE step. Do not push. | User's request | `git log` shows each step's commit and the `spe-r03` tag. |
| R3.7 | Give every prediction a band. A hit means the measured number falls inside the band. | Decision | `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` has a band on every number. |

### Open decisions (go into `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default if you do not answer at approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Gold category rule for mixed billing and outage tickets | User | If any service is down, the category is outage. Otherwise it is billing. Priority follows the outage severity. |
| D2 | Drop D or keep it with a retry cap that fixes F6 | User | Drop D. |
| D3 | Whether the hard set counts toward the stop rule | Claude | Yes. Every predicted cell counts. |

### Updates to `spe/failures.md`

- F4: Fix becomes "P1, split the status check out of the merged tool (r03)". It stays open until round 3 results confirm the fix.
- F5: Fixed. Add the R3.5 selftest case so the bug cannot come back.
- F6: Fix becomes "Not fixed. Config D dropped in r03. Reopen this if D returns."

## 2. Predict

Grader checks:
- Category accuracy: `grade.py` checks for an exact match of `label.category` against the gold category.
- Priority accuracy: `grade.py` checks for an exact match of `label.priority` against the gold priority.
- No LLM judge is used. Both metrics are code checks.

Cost: I log cost for A, B, and C but do not predict it. The pasted log has a round 2 cost only for D, so there is no baseline for the other configs.

### Core set (round 2 tickets)

| Metric | Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Band | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.86 | ± 0.05 | A does not change. The only difference is 5 trials instead of 3. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.86 | ± 0.05 | B does not change. My round 2 reason for a gain did not hold, so I dropped it. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.80 | 0.83 | ± 0.05 | Restoring the status check should fix outage tickets that were put in the wrong category. I stop below 0.84 because the other merged tools stay in place. |
| priority accuracy | C | 0.71 | 0.76 | ± 0.05 | F4 sent outage tickets to P3. Restoring the lookup should close most of the 0.07 gap to round 1's 0.78. |

### Hard set (10 new tickets, no round 2 baseline)

There is no round 2 number for these tickets. The naive guess is the config's core-set number.

| Metric | Config | Naive guess | Predicted | Band | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.70 | ± 0.10 | Mixed tickets have two plausible categories. I expect a drop of about 0.15 from the core set. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.70 | ± 0.10 | The same reason applies. A and B were equal on the core set. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.80 | 0.70 | ± 0.10 | The status check helps on the outage half of each ticket. I expect that to offset C's lower core-set score. |
| priority accuracy | C | 0.71 | 0.65 | ± 0.10 | Severity is harder to judge when billing and outage text are mixed in one ticket. |

## 3. Evaluate

### Harness gates (all must pass before launch)

1. **Grader selftest.** The oracle passes. An empty answer fails. A wrong answer fails. The R3.5 case scores `label.priority`.
2. **Control regrade.** Regrade the round 2 transcripts with the current `grade.py`. The results must match the regraded round 2 numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, and priority C 0.71. If any number differs, I halt and report.
3. **Label check.** All 10 hard tickets have a gold category and a gold priority under the D1 rule.
4. **Dry run.** Run 1 trial on each of 3 cells: A on core T01, C on core T17, and B on hard H01. Each trial must pass the schema check. C on T17 must call the status tool. No transcript may touch graders, answers, or predictions.

### Workflow arguments (`spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`)

- `ROUND = 3`. This is the only place the round number appears. Prompt text reads it from this constant.
- `configs: [A, B, C]`
- `sets: { core: 30 tickets, hard: 10 tickets }`
- `trialsPerCell: 5`
- `splitCellExtraTrials: 3 per cell`. A cell is split when its 5 trials disagree on the answer. Extra trials are capped at 60 in total.
- `trialSchema: { category, priority, tool_calls, tokens, cost }`
- Peek scan: void any trial whose transcript reads a grader, answer, or prediction path.
- `budgetCapUSD: 20`. Skip any trial that would cross the cap and log the skip.
- The run ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

The run is 40 tickets × 3 configs × 5 trials = 600 trials, plus up to 60 extra trials. I estimate about $0.015 per trial. That figure scales D's round 2 cost of $0.004 up for larger models, and it is a guess. The total is about $9 to $10. The cap is $20.

### Halt conditions

I halt and report if any of these happen:
- The budget cap is hit.
- The control regrade does not match.
- A trial reads the answer key.
- The grader selftest fails.
- D1 is still unanswered when the hard-set labels are needed.

## 4. Order of work after approval

1. Save your message verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the round 3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Write D1 to D3 into `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Apply the updates to `spe/failures.md`. Commit as `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1-P4, split C status tool, hard set, drop D, n=5`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It contains:
   - round 3 and date 2026-10-21
   - author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"
   - configs A, B, and C
   - each number with its band and its Why
   - `same_as_last_round`
   Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit as `SPE r03 predict: core A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.83 / prio C 0.76, hard set 0.70`.
3. Build the harness and pass the gates. Commit as `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, commit as `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out:
   - Add the round 3 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md`, with a "Which Why broke" section under them. If the naive guess was closer, I will say so plainly.
   - Add new F-numbers to `spe/failures.md`.
   - Add a "Proposed for round 4" table to the spec.
   - Write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`.
   - Commit as `SPE r03 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r03`.

Commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.
